en.headline: Customs seizes 200 live crickets and 13kg of cockroaches at Lo Wu
en.dek: Two travellers were arrested after officers found the insects, commonly used as pet feed, in their baggage at the border checkpoint over the weekend.
body: Hong Kong Customs said it had intercepted two travellers in separate cases at the Lo Wu Control Point for allegedly importing live insects without authorisation.

On Saturday officers stopped a 71-year-old local man in the arrival hall and seized 200 live crickets valued at about HK$2,000 from his baggage. The following day a 66-year-old local woman was stopped at the same checkpoint carrying 13 kilograms of live Dubia cockroaches valued at about HK$3,900.

Both were arrested. The cases have been referred to the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department for further investigation. Customs reminded the public that importing any plant pest or plant infected by such pests without a permit from the Director of Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation is an offence punishable by a maximum fine of HK$10,000 and six months’ imprisonment.

zh.headline: 海關羅湖檢200隻活蟋蟀及13公斤蟑螂 拘兩旅客
zh.dek: 海關周末在羅湖管制站截獲兩名旅客，行李內分別藏有活體蟋蟀及杜比亞蟑螂，估計市值共約5,900元，兩人已被捕。
body: 香港海關表示，過去兩日在羅湖管制站偵破兩宗懷疑非法進口活體植物病蟲害案件，共檢獲200隻活體蟋蟀及13公斤活體杜比亞蟑螂，估計市值合共約5,900元，拘捕兩名抵港旅客。
本月5日，關員在入境大堂截查一名71歲本地男子，在其行李發現200隻懷疑非法進口活體蟋蟀，估計市值約2,000元。翌日再於同一地點截查一名66歲本地女子，在行李檢獲13公斤懷疑非法進口活體杜比亞蟑螂，估計市值約3,900元。
兩案已轉交漁農自然護理署跟進。海關提醒，任何人未事先獲得漁護署署長授權而將任何植物病蟲害或受感染植物進口，即屬違法，一經定罪最高可罰款1萬元及監禁6個月。
